A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 37-page primer, including its figures, tables, equations, and Appendix A. Text extraction and visual inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Although primarily a primer, v3 reports an author-attributed qualitative empirical finding in Section 3.4: weight/memory decay hurt performance in certain reinforcement-learning game environments. This is labeled unpublished work; scores and experimental details are not provided.

after.justification: V5 retains the same author-attributed unpublished finding about detrimental weight/memory decay in reinforcement-learning game environments. This qualitative empirical outcome qualifies despite the absence of numerical scores.

M1.justification: The FWP architectures, update rules, objectives, and proposed neurobiological implementation are unchanged. The added hypernetwork footnote provides background on existing models.

E1.justification: No training or evaluation datasets or task scenarios are added or removed. The authors' qualitative reinforcement-learning observation concerns the same unspecified game environments in both versions.

E2.justification: Section 3.4 retains the same DeltaNet/Gated DeltaNet discussion and cited performance comparisons. The newly cited hypernetwork and neuroscience models are not evaluated as additional comparators.

E3.justification: No evaluation metrics, splits, budgets, sample sizes, or testing procedures are revised. Both versions leave the protocol for the unpublished reinforcement-learning observation unspecified.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or case studies are added or removed. The weight-decay observation and existing illustrative memory and expressivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals, or significance tests for the authors' qualitative empirical finding. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The reported harmful effect of decay in some reinforcement-learning games is unchanged. The cited performance findings and Table 2's qualitative memory-system comparisons also remain unchanged; no empirical result entries are added or revised.

T1.justification: The formal definitions, FWP–transformer derivations, and Appendix A's local-loss derivations are unchanged after matching page reflow. The new historical remark about linear regression adds no formal derivation or revision to the mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, main introductory claims, and conclusion retain the same contributions: explaining FWPs and their connections to sequence models, local learning, and synaptic plasticity.

C2.justification: The rewritten fast/slow-weight footnote preserves the existing exception for fully online updates. Biological interpretations, retrieval tradeoffs, applicability arguments, and limitations remain unchanged; the new gain-modulation footnote primarily adds related-work context.

D1.justification: Guidance on SiLU followed by L2 normalization, chunk-wise training, and access to flash-linear-attention implementations is unchanged. No reproducibility details are added for the unpublished reinforcement-learning observation.

R1.justification: V5 adds ten references supporting two new footnotes: historical least-squares antecedents and links between gain-modulating hypernetworks and computational neuroscience. Examples include Legendre, Stigler, Perez et al., Jayakumar et al., Rao, and Costacurta et al. This is a limited expansion of research positioning.

P1.justification: V5 adds an introductory historical footnote and a hypernetwork footnote in Section 3.2, and rewrites the existing fast/slow terminology note. Section order and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Added footnotes and bibliography entries cause limited page reflow. Appendix A begins below the final references on page 35 in v5, whereas it starts at the top in v3. Figures 1–2 and Tables 1–2 retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: The new Section 3.2 footnote gives readers a more explicit, referenced connection between FWPs, gain modulation, and computational neuroscience; the introductory footnote also qualifies the historical account. These are useful, limited improvements for an interdisciplinary primer. Its technical exposition, empirical support, and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
